items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names and doc comments are mostly clear. The unexplained alias `type ConsistentHashSourceIp = ConsistentHashSourceIP` adds a confusing second name for the same type. The custom `UnmarshalJSON` on the API type has no comment saying why it is needed.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: It follows the plugin pattern (consistent_hash.go IR, apply step, merge func) and the generated code came from `make go-generate-apis`. Weak points: the `ConsistentHashSourceIp` alias is dead code, and the API type has a hand-written `UnmarshalJSON` (float64 ttl), which doesn't match the CRD's string schema.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: There is CEL validation plus MinLength on key fields. But the merge path does `if err == nil { p1.spec.consistentHash.hashPolicies = hashPolicies }`, so a rebuild error is dropped without logging. `UnmarshalJSON` also truncates float ttl values silently.

items.name: Multi-policy merge semantics
items.evidence: A dedicated merge function in merge.go unions the arrays with the higher-priority policy first, dedupes, re-sorts into canonical order, handles disable, and calls `mergeOrigins.Append("consistentHash", p2Ref, p2MergeOrigins)`. A merge golden test was added and the hidden tests pass.

items.name: Empty spec and disable handling
items.name_zh: 空配置与 disable 处理
items.evidence: The CEL rule `!has(self.disable) || !self.disable || (!has(self.headers)...)` shows up in the generated CRD YAML. The apply step sets `action.HashPolicy = nil` when disable is true, and the empty-spec default is covered. Hidden tests pass.
